chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abdullah ibn Bahrr from a man from Zurarah said:
I asked: 'The fish leaps out of the water, falls onto the shore, and writhes until it dies.' He said, 'Eat it.'

Because the prohibition in those reports is directed only at what dies in the water, and this report implies that the fish comes out alive and then dies, and there is no contradiction between them, provided that when it exits the water alive, one must ensure that the one who catches it catches it while it is still alive and then it dies; otherwise, if it dies before he catches it, it is not permissible to eat it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish that die on land after leaping out of the water?
ai.summary: This narration from Zurarah clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between fish that die in water (which are generally prohibited) and those that leap out alive and perish on land (which are permissible). The ruling hinges on the condition that the fish must be captured while still alive; if it dies before being caught, it becomes non-permissible, illustrating the Shia principle of linking permissibility to the state of life at the moment of capture.
